COSMOLOGICAL DATA ANALYSIS¶

04 — WMAP9 + DESI DR1 JOINT ΛCDM FITTING¶

Author: Cherian Parangot Ittyipe
Thesis DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17681763
Repository: github.com/Cherian-pi/wmap9-desi-joint-lcdm (Soon Uploaded to Github)
Chain: wmap9_desi_joint_flat_20260628_004948.npy
Status: Fully converged - 32 walkers × 1000 steps, 30,400 post-burn-in samples. (Can be analysed by increasing the number of steps and walkers, so that parameters can be constrained to a better precised values.)

1. PURPOSE¶

This notebook combines the official WMAP nine year CMB Likelihood with the DESI Data Release 1 (DR1) baryon acoustic oscillation measurements under flat ΛCDM. It is a joint assembling of the two independently validated dataset legs into a single joint posterior.

The WMAP + DESI combination is not competitive wih Planck + DESI, but it can help to build and validate the cosmological parameter analysis from the scratch that including validating the convergences of the chains, developing an idea on the bugs during the evaluation, which are generally can be used to building other pipelines.

Key rule¶

No Planck rᵈ prior is used. WMAP9 already calibrates rᵈ through the CMB acoustic peaks. Adding a Planck rᵈ prior would contaminate the joint result with Planck information.

Why the datasets are complementary¶

WMAP9 has degeneracies between H₀ and Ωch² along the acoustic scale direction. DESI BAO breaks this degeneracy by measuring H₀rᵈ and Ωm at low redshift. The joint posterior is tighter than either dataset alone on H₀ and Ωm.

Prior bounds — widened from Notebook 02¶

The WMAP9-only notebook used tight bounds [60, 80] on H₀. Here we widen to [55, 85] to allow the joint posterior to move freely.

2 JOINT LIKELIHOOD¶

2.1 Structure¶

The Joint log-posterior add two independent likelihoods.

ln L_total(θ) = ln L_WMAP9(θ) + ln L_DESI_BAO($Ω_{bh}^2, Ω_{ch}^2 , H_0$)

θ = [$Ω_{bh}^2$, $Ω_{ch}²$, $H_0, n_s, ln(10^{10} A_s), 𝝉$]

WMAP9 constrains all 6 parameters via the CMB power spectra. DESI DR1 BAO constrains $Ω_{bh}^2, Ω_{ch}^2, H_0$ via distance ratios DM/rd and DH/rd. $n_s, A_s, τ$ are insensitive to BAO and remain determined by WMAP9 alone.

2.2 Parameter Sensitivity¶

  • WMAP9 constrains all 6 parameters via CMB power spectra.
  • DESI DR1 BAO constrains $Ω_{bh}^2 ,Ω_{ch}^2, H_0$ via distance ratios DM/rd and DH/rd.
  • $n_s, A_s, 𝛕$ are insensitive to BAO. So they remain determined by WMAP9 Alone

2.3 Key rule : No planck $r^d$ prior¶

No Planck $r^d$ prior is used. WMAP9 already calibrates $r^d$ through the CMB acoustic peaks. Adding a Planck rᵈ prior would contaminate the joint result with Planck information.

2.4 Complementary Data Sets¶

  • WMAP9 alone has a broad degeneracy between $H_0$ and $Ω_{ch}^2$ degeneracy.
  • DESI BAO can break the degeneracy between $H_0$ and $\Omega_{ch}$.
  • The joint posterior can provide tighter constraints on the cosmological parameters.

2.5 Prior Ranges¶

The priors are taken from the References articles, | Parameters| Prior Bounds| |---|---| |$\Omega_{bh}$| [0.018, 0.028]| |$\Omega_{ch}$| [0.08, 0.16]| |$H_{O}$| [55, 85]| |$n_s$ | [0.9, 1.05]| |$ln_{10} A_s$| [2.9 ,3.3]| |$\tau$ | [0.03 ,0.18] |

Cell 2 — Load WMAP9 Likelihood Library¶

The official WMAP9 Fortran library (libwmap9.so) is loaded via Python's ctypes. The library evaluates all official likelihood components:

  • TT high-$\ell$ MASTER
  • TT low-$\ell$ Gibbs sampling
  • TT low-$\ell$ determinant
  • TE high-$\ell$ chi-squared
  • TE high-$\ell$ determinant
  • Low-$\ell$ TT/TE/EE/BB chi-squared
  • Low-$\ell$ TT/TE/EE/BB determinant

COMP_NAMES = [
    'TT high-l MASTER', 'TT low-l Gibbs', 'TT low-l det', 'Beam+ptsrc',

def wmap_like(cltt, clte, clee, clbb):
    """
    Official WMAP9 likelihood.
    Inputs : Dl arrays shape (1199,), ell=2..1200, muK^2.
    Returns: (total -2lnL, component vector shape (8,))
    """
    def a(x): return np.ascontiguousarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    lk = np.zeros(NUM_WMAP, dtype=np.float64)
    fn_compute(
        a(cltt).ctypes.data_as(DPA), a(clte).ctypes.data_as(DPA),
        a(clee).ctypes.data_as(DPA), a(clbb).ctypes.data_as(DPA),
        lk.ctypes.data_as(DPA)
    )
    return 2.0 * lk.sum(), 2.0 * lk

Cell 3 — CAMB Theory Engine (WMAP9 side)¶

Returns Dl arrays for ell=2..1200 as required by the WMAP9 Fortran library.

In [4]:
ELL_WMAP = np.arange(2, 1201)   # length 1199

def get_cls_camb_wmap(ombh2, omch2, H0, ns, ln10As, tau):
    """
    Compute lensed CMB Dl spectra for WMAP9 likelihood.
    Returns TT, TE, EE, BB each shape (1199,) for ell=2..1200 in muK^2.
    """
    cp = camb.CAMBparams()
    cp.set_cosmology(H0=H0, ombh2=ombh2, omch2=omch2, tau=tau)
    cp.InitPower.set_params(ns=ns, As=np.exp(ln10As) * 1e-10)
    cp.set_for_lmax(1250, lens_potential_accuracy=0)
    res = camb.get_results(cp)
    Dl  = res.get_cmb_power_spectra(cp, CMB_unit='muK', raw_cl=False)['total']
    return Dl[ELL_WMAP, 0], Dl[ELL_WMAP, 3], Dl[ELL_WMAP, 1], Dl[ELL_WMAP, 2]

## Cell 4 — Load DESI DR1 BAO Data

def load_mean_labeled(filepath):
    """Returns {quantity_name: value}, immune to row ordering in the file."""
    out = {}
    with open(filepath) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                continue
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) < 3:
                continue
            try:
                out[parts[2]] = float(parts[1])
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return out


def load_cov(filepath):
    rows = []
    with open(filepath) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                continue
            try:
                rows.append([float(x) for x in line.split()])
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return np.array(rows)

Cell 5 — CAMB BAO Theory Engine¶

Computes DM/rd, DH/rd, DV/rd at each tracer redshift.

In [7]:
def get_bao_theory(ombh2, omch2, H0, zeff, mode):
    """
    Compute BAO observables at zeff.
    Returns ([DM/rd, DH/rd], rd) for mode='aniso'
    Returns ([DV/rd],        rd) for mode='iso'
    """
    pars = camb.CAMBparams()
    pars.set_cosmology(H0=H0, ombh2=ombh2, omch2=omch2,
                       mnu=0.06, omk=0.0, tau=0.054)
    pars.set_dark_energy()
    pars.InitPower.set_params(As=2.1e-9, ns=0.965)
    pars.set_for_lmax(500, lens_potential_accuracy=0)
    results = camb.get_results(pars)

    rd  = results.get_derived_params()['rdrag']
    DA  = results.angular_diameter_distance(zeff)
    DM  = DA * (1.0 + zeff)
    H_z = results.hubble_parameter(zeff)
    DH  = 299792.458 / H_z
    DV  = (zeff * DM**2 * DH) ** (1.0 / 3.0)

    if mode == 'aniso':
        return np.array([DM / rd, DH / rd]), rd
    else:
        return np.array([DV / rd]), rd

Cell 6 — Individual Log-Likelihoods¶

In [8]:
def log_like_wmap9(theta):
    """
    WMAP9 CMB log-likelihood.
    Uses all 6 parameters: ombh2, omch2, H0, ns, ln10As, tau.
    """
    try:
        neg2, _ = wmap_like(*get_cls_camb_wmap(*theta))
        return -0.5 * neg2 if np.isfinite(neg2) else -np.inf
    except Exception:
        return -np.inf


def log_like_desi(ombh2, omch2, H0):
    """
    DESI DR1 BAO Gaussian likelihood.
    Only uses ombh2, omch2, H0. nS, As, tau do not affect BAO distances.
    No Planck rd prior — WMAP9 already calibrates rd via the CMB.
    """
    lnL = 0.0
    for name, d in bao_data.items():
        try:
            theory, _ = get_bao_theory(ombh2, omch2, H0, d['zeff'], d['mode'])
        except Exception:
            return -np.inf
        delta = d['mean'] - theory
        lnL  -= 0.5 * float(delta @ d['icov'] @ delta)
    return lnL if np.isfinite(lnL) else -np.inf


# Test both at WMAP9 best-fit
theta_wmap = np.array([0.02264, 0.1138, 70.0, 0.972, 3.089, 0.089])
ll_w = log_like_wmap9(theta_wmap)
ll_d = log_like_desi(theta_wmap[0], theta_wmap[1], theta_wmap[2])

Cell 7 — Joint Prior and Posterior¶

In [9]:
def log_prior(theta):
    """Flat prior within bounds."""
    if np.all((theta >= PRIOR_BOUNDS[:, 0]) & (theta <= PRIOR_BOUNDS[:, 1])):
        return 0.0
    return -np.inf


def log_posterior_joint(theta):
    """
    Joint WMAP9 + DESI DR1 log-posterior.

    ln L_total = ln L_WMAP9(theta) + ln L_DESI_BAO(ombh2, omch2, H0)

    No Planck rd prior. WMAP9 provides the early-universe calibration
    of the sound horizon through the CMB acoustic peaks.
    DESI contributes only through ombh2, omch2, H0.
    """
    lp = log_prior(theta)
    if not np.isfinite(lp):
        return -np.inf

    # WMAP9 CMB — all 6 parameters
    ll_wmap = log_like_wmap9(theta)
    if not np.isfinite(ll_wmap):
        return -np.inf

    # DESI BAO — only ombh2, omch2, H0
    ll_desi = log_like_desi(theta[0], theta[1], theta[2])
    if not np.isfinite(ll_desi):
        return -np.inf

    return lp + ll_wmap + ll_desi


# Test joint posterior at WMAP9 best-fit
lp_test = log_posterior_joint(theta_wmap)
print(f'Joint log-posterior at WMAP9 BF: {lp_test:.2f}')
print(f'  = prior {log_prior(theta_wmap):.1f} + WMAP9 {ll_w:.2f} + DESI {ll_d:.2f}')

import time

def neg_log_posterior_joint(theta):
    val = log_posterior_joint(theta)
    return 1e10 if not np.isfinite(val) else -val

# Start from WMAP9 best-fit

print('Single evaluation time test...')
t0 = time.time()
_ = neg_log_posterior_joint(theta0)
t_single = time.time() - t0
print(f'Single eval: {t_single:.2f} s')
print(f'Estimated MCMC: ~{t_single * NWALKERS * NSTEPS / 3600:.1f} hours')

print('\nRunning MAP optimisation...')
result = opt.minimize(
    neg_log_posterior_joint, theta0, method='Nelder-Mead',
    options=dict(xatol=1e-4, fatol=1e-2, maxiter=2000, disp=True)
)

print('\nApproximate G-R R-hat (walker groups):')
for i, name in enumerate(PARAM_NAMES):
    gm   = [post_burn[:, j*group_sz:(j+1)*group_sz, i].mean() for j in range(n_groups)]
    gv   = [post_burn[:, j*group_sz:(j+1)*group_sz, i].var()  for j in range(n_groups)]
    W    = np.mean(gv)
    B    = np.var(gm) * len(post_burn)
    n    = len(post_burn)
    Rhat = np.sqrt(((n-1)/n * W + B/n) / W) if W > 0 else np.nan
    print(f'  R-hat({name:8s}) = {Rhat:.4f}  [{"OK" if Rhat < 1.05 else "check"}]')

# Smoothing: smooth_scale is the kernel width in units of bin size when
# positive — small positive values (e.g. 0.4) give LESS smoothing, not more.
# Use a larger positive value, or a negative value to let GetDist pick the
# bandwidth automatically (scaled by abs(value); -1 is GetDist's own default).
samples_joint.updateSettings({
    'smooth_scale_2D': 1.9,   # try 0.8–2.0; higher = smoother contours
    'smooth_scale_1D': 0.9,   # try 0.3–1.0; higher = smoother 1D curves

## GetDist Multi-Analysis Posterior Comparison
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from getdist import MCSamples, plots as gdplots
BASE      = '/Users/cherianpi/Desktop/WMAP+DESI'
LIKE_DIR  = BASE + '/wmap_likelihood_v5'
PY_DIR    = BASE + '/Python files'
SO_PATH   = PY_DIR + '/libwmap9.so'
BAO_DIR   = BASE + '/bao_data'
CHAIN_DIR = PY_DIR + '/chains'
IMG_DIR   = PY_DIR + '/Images'
CHAIN_DIR = Path(BASE + '/Python files/chains')

PARAM_NAMES_FULL  = ['ombh2', 'omch2', 'H0', 'ns', 'ln10As', 'tau']
PARAM_LABELS_FULL = [r'\Omega_b h^2', r'\Omega_c h^2', 'H_0',
                      'n_s', r'\ln(10^{10}A_s)', r'\tau']
PARAM_NAMES_BAO   = ['ombh2', 'omch2', 'H0']
PARAM_LABELS_BAO  = [r'\Omega_b h^2', r'\Omega_c h^2', 'H_0']


def load_flat(path, burn_frac=0.1):
    """Auto-detects raw (steps, walkers, dim) vs already-flat (N, dim) chains."""
    arr = np.load(path)
    if arr.ndim == 3:
        nsteps, nwalkers, ndim = arr.shape
        burn = max(1, int(nsteps * burn_frac))
        return arr[burn:].reshape(-1, ndim)
    elif arr.ndim == 2:
        return arr
    raise ValueError(f'Unexpected shape {arr.shape} for {path}')


wmap9 = load_flat(CHAIN_DIR / 'wmap9_lcdm_flat_samples_20260614_235110.npy')
joint = load_flat(CHAIN_DIR / 'wmap9_desi_joint_flat_20260628_004948.npy')
desi  = load_flat(CHAIN_DIR / 'desi_bao_lcdm_flat_20260615_184435.npy')

print(f'WMAP9 alone        : {wmap9.shape}')
print(f'WMAP9 + DESI Joint : {joint.shape}')
print(f'DESI DR2 (rd prior): {desi.shape}')

samples_wmap9 = MCSamples(samples=wmap9, names=PARAM_NAMES_FULL,
                           labels=PARAM_LABELS_FULL, label='WMAP9 alone')
samples_joint = MCSamples(samples=joint, names=PARAM_NAMES_FULL,
                           labels=PARAM_LABELS_FULL, label='WMAP9 + DESI Joint')
samples_desi  = MCSamples(samples=desi, names=PARAM_NAMES_BAO,
                           labels=PARAM_LABELS_BAO, label='DESI DR2 BAO (rd prior)')

# Add derived Omega_m to each — the one quantity that's genuinely
# comparable across all three analyses regardless of parameterisation
for s, names in [(samples_wmap9, PARAM_NAMES_FULL),
                  (samples_joint, PARAM_NAMES_FULL),
                  (samples_desi, PARAM_NAMES_BAO)]:
    ombh2 = s.samples[:, names.index('ombh2')]
    omch2 = s.samples[:, names.index('omch2')]
    H0    = s.samples[:, names.index('H0')]
    Om = (ombh2 + omch2) / (H0 / 100) ** 2
    s.addDerived(Om, name='Omegam', label=r'\Omega_m')

for s in [samples_wmap9, samples_joint, samples_desi]:
    s.updateSettings({'smooth_scale_2D': 0.6, 'smooth_scale_1D': 0.4})

# ── Plot 1: full 6-parameter triangle — WMAP9 alone vs Joint only ──────────
# (DESI BAO-only has no constraint on ns/As/tau, so it's excluded here

def print_margestats(samples, label):
    stats = samples.getMargeStats()
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print(label)
    print("="*60)

    for name in ['ombh2', 'omch2', 'H0', 'ns', 'ln10As', 'tau']:
        p = stats.parWithName(name)
        print(f"{name:8s} = {p.mean:.5f} ± {p.err:.5f}")
